reviews.review_description:
The Mars environment is pleasant to explore, and the stylized, cartoony art suits it well. Highlights for me were an air hockey match against an AI and riding a robotic camel across the Martian landscape. The holograms are a smart touch: the closer you try to get to your family, the more they stutter and break apart, which makes the distance feel real. Underneath the sci-fi, it’s a nice reminder of why work-life balance matters.

It’s a good length, and the branching choices make me want to replay it.

One issue: near the end, the game soft-locked after a key interaction, and I had to reload a checkpoint about 20 minutes back. Hopefully that gets patched.

Overall, it’s a heartfelt little VR story with some memorable ideas.

developer_response.body:
Thank you for such a thoughtful and detailed review! It's especially rewarding to hear that you enjoyed exploring Mars, including some of our more playful moments with the air hockey and robotic camel!

We're particularly glad you noticed the holographic interactions. The fragility of those connections was a deliberate creative choice, designed to make the emotional distance between Natalie and her family something you can actually experience, rather than simply observe. It's wonderful to hear that this resonated with you.

We're also sorry about the soft-lock you encountered. That's certainly not the experience we intended, and our development team will investigate this further.

Knowing that the story stays with players beyond the headset means a great deal to our team. We hope your next journey through Mars reveals a few more surprises!

reviews.review_description: An imaginative, genuinely story-driven game with an unexpected take on sci-fi. It has the spirit of an indie narrative adventure, with a distinctive story that makes you want to keep playing. If you enjoy something a little offbeat that takes storytelling seriously without losing its sense of humor, give it a go.

No player adjusments, smooth turn ect, needs crouch, trigger for run? no. Obvious avoidable problems other developers have already smoothed over so new projects like this could avoid. However it seems this developer will stumble through these dumb problems, instead of learning from more experienced developers.
i have hope that during early development means things could be fixed. Lets hope. . .

developer_response.body:
Thank you for taking the time to share your feedback with us.

We really appreciate the suggestion regarding a crouch feature, and we’re glad to let you know that crouch functionality, along with further player movement refinements, is planned for upcoming updates

We also wanted to clarify that running is currently assigned to the trigger. Regarding motion speed, we purposefully design movement to accommodate a less progressive motion comfort. We recognize that for many players, fast or sudden movement across environments can cause discomfort, so we aimed to achieve a balance that feels both responsive and comfortable.

Your input helps us refine the experience, so thank you again for playing and sharing your thoughts to help us improve!

reviews.review_title: Really nice story and unique experience
reviews.review_description:
If you're looking for something unique, this is it!
It felt less like playing a game and more like stepping inside a movie where your choices actually matter.
Great storytelling and super immersive.
Highly recommend!

developer_response.body: Thank you so much for these kind words! ❤️ We set out to create an experience that blurs the line between a game and a film, where you feel truly present in the story and your choices matter. It means a lot to hear that this resonated with you. We’re just getting started on this journey, and we’re excited to grow the WinterOver community with players like you. Welcome aboard, and thank you for being part of it!

reviews.review_description: Great vr story  driven game, wow I'm really loving this so much, I'm going to restart the whole game and play it from the beginning, it's really good 👍 p.s I would like a Crouch button.

developer_response.body: Thank you so much! 🙌 Hearing that you’re enjoying WinterOver so much that you want to jump back in and experience the story all over again is incredibly rewarding for our team. And thanks for the crouch button suggestion! We really appreciate players sharing their ideas as we continue to build and improve the experience. Keep the feedback coming, and welcome to the WinterOver community! 🚀

reviews.review_description: Engaging little interactive story and great use of the medium. I know this has been in development for a while and glad to see it published.

A short little narrative game. Some unique vr scenarios in there that were pretty cool but basic for the most part. It's not an exceptional story. It's not too bad and not too great, I would say. It's a bit pricey for what you get. I think £11.99 would have been the ideal price to pay perhaps.

developer_response.body: Thank you for playing and taking the time to review our game! We appreciate your honest feedback on the story, VR mechanics, and pricing. Balancing content scope with price point is really important to us, and feedback like yours is super helpful as we evaluate future updates and projects. Thanks again for your support!
